claims.text: United States Vice President JD Vance declined to offer a timeline for the end of the US-Israeli war on Iran.
US Vice President JD Vance stated: "I wouldn't call it a war. Right now, there is no active shooting."
US Vice President JD Vance stated that major combat operations against Iran lasted about six weeks.
Roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas flowed through the Strait of Hormuz prior to the war.
US Vice President JD Vance stated a deal transferring control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves to the US would help lower global oil costs.
An attack on a wedding party in Sirik, Iran, reportedly killed at least five people and injured nearly 70 others.
An air strike on an Iranian elementary school in Minab killed more than 150 people on the first day of the war.
As of August, 18 US service members have been killed and 750 wounded in the conflict with Iran.
US Vice President JD Vance said "sometimes things happen" when asked if an American strike was responsible for deaths at an Iranian wedding.
The Iranian Red Crescent reported that four people were killed and more than 50 wounded when missile shrapnel struck a home during a wedding in Kuhestak.
Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna called Vice President Vance's statements "unbelievable gaslighting."
US President Donald Trump wrote on social media that the US has "virtually unlimited" amounts of mid- to high-grade munitions.
A February 28 US air attack in Minab killed at least 156 people, mostly schoolchildren.
US President Donald Trump called reports of dwindling US ammunition supplies "100% wrong" and described those spreading them as "treasonous."
Reuters reported on August 4 that the US military has used virtually all of its ATACMS and PrSM surface-to-surface missile stockpiles during the war with Iran.
Military leaders warned President Donald Trump in recent weeks that US supplies of Patriot missile interceptors were falling.
US Central Command launched attacks targeting Iranian air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, and mine laying capabilities.
Jordan reported detecting 13 ballistic missiles in its airspace, 10 of which it intercepted.
The United States unveiled measures on August 19 to tighten its financial siege and blockade around Iran's ports.
Mojtaba Khamenei appointed Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps founder Mohsen Rezaee as his representative on Iran's Supreme National Security Council.
Two additional Australians were confirmed safe after the Nepal-Tibet floods, reducing the number of missing Australians to 36.
More than 1,200 people have been confirmed dead and over 5,500 remain missing following the Nepal-Tibet floods.
Unicef warned that at least 22,000 children in Nepal urgently need safe drinking water and better sanitation.
Helicopters airlifted more than 4,000 people across Rasuwa and Nuwakot following the August 26 Bhote Koshi-Trishuli flood in Nepal.
Captain Bimal Sharma of Simrik Air stated that flood rescue missions in the Trishuli gorge were tougher than Everest-season flying due to missing landing spots and inaccurate coordinates.
Nepal flood victims are set to be identified through DNA testing.
Rescuers used rafts and drones to search for survivors trapped inside hydro tunnels along Nepal's Trishuli River.
A glacial collapse in the Himalayas triggered flash flooding and debris flows across the Nepal-Tibet border.
Critics have described the multi-billion-dollar US oil agreement in Venezuela as modern-day colonialism.
Venezuelan opposition figure María Corina Machado called for a democratic transition following the US-Venezuela oil deal.
The US-Venezuela agreement grants the United States access to more than 65 billion barrels of oil in Venezuela.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright traveled to Venezuela to oversee agreement signings with Chevron, GE Vernova, and ENI.
Interim leader Delcy Rodriguez estimated Venezuela will make $209 billion in profit from the energy deals over 25 years.
María Corina Machado stated that "the wealth of our subsoil does not belong to an illegitimate regime – it belongs to the Venezuelan people."
Delcy Rodríguez assumed power as interim president in January after former president Nicolás Maduro was abducted by US special forces.
Venezuela possesses the world's largest proven crude oil reserves, estimated at 303 billion barrels.
US energy companies signed multi-billion-dollar deals with Venezuela after control of significant oil assets was granted to the US.
Chevron made a $7 billion bet on Venezuela's oil industry.
The disappearance of anchovies along the South American Pacific coast is signaling a major El Niño event.
UK Met Office projections indicate equatorial Pacific ocean temperatures could spike by 3 degrees Celsius when El Niño peaks in late 2026 or early 2027.

WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo stated: "Never before in the 50-year history of the WMO have we launched such a major mobilisation delivering forecasts and services to save lives and livelihoods."
The British government is planning a public campaign advising citizens to stock up on tinned food and water for national emergencies.
Ocean temperatures at the center of El Niño measured 2.6 degrees Celsius above the 30-year average, with models forecasting a peak of 4 degrees Celsius in November.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that "El Niño is being supersized before our eyes."
The World Food Programme estimated that El Niño is likely to push about 50 million people into acute hunger.
Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded over 50,000 cases of respiratory infections linked to wildfires between July and August, including more than 12,000 cases in children under five.
Professor Bambang Hero Saharjo stated research indicates this year's El Niño could cause wildfires to burn up to 11 million hectares in Indonesia.
The World Meteorological Organization warned that the current El Niño could be the strongest recorded since records began four decades ago.
An Israeli drone strike in Gaza City's Rimal neighborhood killed one person and injured several others.
Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir presented a plan aiming to remove roughly two million Palestinians from the Gaza Strip over seven years.
The Gaza Health Ministry reports that at least 73,470 people have been killed in Gaza since October 2023, including over 1,330 since the October ceasefire.
Israeli forces and settlers shot dead 16-year-old Khalil Abu Alia and 19-year-old Omar al-Nassan in the West Bank village of al-Mughayyir.
Israeli troops demolished homes belonging to 12 Palestinian families in Khirbet al-Taban, leaving 70 residents homeless.
Human rights group B'Tselem stated that Khirbet al-Taban is the 66th Palestinian community wiped off the map since October 2023.
The UN recorded that at least 81 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year.
Israeli police arrested a 19-year-old settler on suspicion of involvement in an attack on the West Bank village of Qusra.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated at a military outpost that Israel controls 60% of Gaza and will not withdraw.
Israel's Deputy Chief of General Staff Maj Gen Tamir Yadai stated that Israel controls 65% of the Gaza Strip.
